transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Ellen (NSM CTO), Marc (Head of ML), Sasha (Security), Tom (Product)

Auto-summary: Draft quality eval plan with golden prompts, regression tests and hallucination checks; agree on metrics and timeline. Redwood to deliver eval plan and run baseline hosted benchmark; customer to share sample data.

00:00 Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call - we have Priya and Lena from our side. Ellen?
00:06 Ellen: Yep here. Marc, Sasha, Tom - all on. Thanks for doing this.
00:12 Jared: Great. The main goal today is to lock down the quality evaluation plan for the POC - golden prompts, regression testing approach, what counts as a pass, and the timeline. Priya will cover the bench details.
00:25 Priya: Thanks. I'll start with an overview. So for NorthStar's clinical-summary assistant, customers told us the non-negotiables are accuracy on factual items (e.g. medications, dates), very low hallucination rate, and strict structure for output - headers, bulleted problems, and follow-up questions. We recommend a three-part eval: golden prompt set, regression tests against known examples, and hallucination/format checks with automated scoring plus manual spot checks.
00:45 Marc: Quick Q - by hallucination do you mean inventing meds or mixing patient identifiers? Those are different severity levels for us.
00:52 Priya: Yes. We'll define severity tiers. Type A is safety-critical (wrong med/dose/date), Type B is moderate (misstated timeline), Type C is cosmetic or phrasing. For the POC success criteria we should set absolute thresholds for Type A (e.g., <0.5% in the golden set) and relative regression tolerance baseline to candidate model.
01:14 Ellen: Sounds right. Also formatting is huge - downstream systems ingest the bulleted output. If it's not parsable, the integration breaks.
01:22 Priya: We'll include format checks - structural validators that ensure required sections exist and field-level regex checks for dates, medication codes, etc.
01:31 Tom: For workload sizing - what do you need from us? average sessions per day, tokens per session?
01:35 Jared: Yes. Ideally: qps target, concurrent sessions, average turns per session, and typical token lengths. That lets us pick model variants and recommend batching/quantization.
01:43 Marc: We can provide two week of traffic: peak qps ~8, p50 tokens/session ~850, p95 ~2300. Concurrent agents around 12. Does that help?
01:52 Priya: That helps a lot. With those numbers we can run a hosted baseline at our default model and then try a quantized LLM on dedicated nodes if you want lower cost per token. But note: quantization can impact hallucination rates slightly, so we should include regression tests.
02:13 Sasha: From security: we require SOC 2 Type II, SSO with SAML, and customer-managed KMS for keys if we do private deployment. Also audit logs retention minimum 1 year. Can Redwood support that during POC?
02:25 Lena: Yes. For hosted POC we can provide SOC 2 documentation and SSO integration guide. For KMS/customer-managed keys that's typically a Private deployment feature, but we can accommodate in a dedicated POC with the right paperwork. We'll share a docs bundle.
02:36 Sasha: Good. Also need to know if transcripts are persisted in plain text and how long.
02:40 Jared: Persistence is configurable; for POC we can set retention to 30 days and enable data-at-rest encryption. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
02:50 Marc: Back to the eval plan - how many golden prompts do you usually use? And how do you ensure they cover edge cases?
02:56 Priya: Typical golden set is 50-150 high-priority prompts. For clinical summaries we'd want a focused set: high-risk cases (polypharmacy, complex histories), tricky formatting, and examples known to trip hallucinations. We'll combine client-provided golden examples with Redwood-curated synthetic edge cases.
03:16 Ellen: Do you do automatic scoring or is it manual? We need a defensible metric for stakeholder sign-off.
03:22 Priya: Both. Automated metrics: token-level F1 for extracting key entities (meds, dates, dosages), strict match for structured fields, BLEU/ROUGE for free text, and hallucination score computed by cross-checking extracted entities against the source. Then manual review - we'll sample 5-10% of outputs for human labeling to catch subtle errors. Final score = weighted combination; we can propose weights (e.g., 50% entity accuracy, 20% hallucination penalty, 20% format compliance, 10% human audit).
03:53 Tom: That breakdown makes sense. Will you share the scoring spreadsheet?
03:56 Jared: Yes - action item, Jared to send the scoring template.
04:00 Marc: On regression tests: do you run across model versions, or is this more prompt-level regression?
04:05 Priya: Both. We'll keep a regression suite of 300-1,000 test cases (mix of golden and large random sample). Each POC iteration we run current model vs baseline and flag regressions by more than X% on key metrics. We also track hallucination delta specifically.
04:22 Marc: What's a reasonable regression threshold to fail the POC?
04:26 Priya: For clinical, conservative thresholds: any increase in Type A hallucinations >0.1% should fail; entity accuracy drop >1% fail. We can calibrate to your risk tolerance.
04:36 Ellen: For reporting, we need per-release artifact - charts and a CSV summary for compliance.
04:41 Priya: We'll produce a dashboard export and a CSV of all test cases with verdicts; also diff reports.
04:48 Sasha: About data: we'll provide anonymized transcripts. Please note PHI removal - we'll scrub identifiers but keep clinical content.
04:55 Jared: Understood. We recommend a hashed ID mapping so you can link back if needed for remediation, but we won't store any raw PHI.
05:03 Tom: Timeline - how long to run the POC end-to-end?
05:07 Jared: Typical POC here is 4-6 weeks: week 0-1 data ingestion and golden prompt finalization, week 2 run baseline hosted benchmarks and initial scoring, week 3 iterate model variants (quantized/dedicated) and run regression, week 4 final analysis & deliverables. If you want dedicated infra we may need extra lead for provisioning (1-2 weeks).
05:30 Marc: We prefer 4 weeks if possible. Budget: are there costs for baseline hosted benchmarks?
05:35 Jared: Baseline hosted benchmark for the POC is usually included; dedicated nodes or extended compute are chargeable. We'll call out any added costs in the proposal.
05:44 Ellen: What about real-time constraints? We need 95th latency < 600ms for short notes.
05:50 Priya: Ok, we'll include latency SLOs in the benchmark. We'll measure p50/p95 end-to-end and token generation latency. If hosted doesn't meet p95, we can suggest dedicated GPU pools or routing policies.
06:02 Marc: Can we test both latest open models and Redwood-verified variants?
06:06 Priya: Yes. We'll run the baseline on Redwood-verified default (hosted) and then try an optimized variant and a quantized candidate. We'll compare accuracy, hallucination, and latency/cost tradeoffs.
06:18 Sasha: For auditing, we need signature of who accessed models and logs. Does Redwood provide audit trail?
06:23 Lena: Yes, audit logs with user/action/resource and timestamps are in the console. We'll document retention and export options.
06:30 Tom: Any guidance on golden prompt wording? We're worried about prompt leakage and overfitting.
06:36 Priya: Best practice: provide 20-50 canonical prompts - keep them representative but not exhaustive. We'll augment with synthetic variations for robustness testing. Also use separate tuning set and a held-out evaluation set to avoid overfitting.
06:51 Marc: For scoring, you mentioned hallucination by cross-checking extracted entities against source - do you run retrieval augmentation or just check against transcript?
06:58 Priya: For the POC we'll check against the provided transcript and structured fields. If you want external retrieval checks (e.g. EMR lookup), that's a separate integration. For now we'll ensure outputs can be validated against the input.
07:10 Ellen: Any gotchas you've seen in clinical settings?
07:13 Priya: Two big ones: 1) models sometimes normalize dates or med names unexpectedly - include strict regex/whitelists; 2) quantization can slightly affect entity generation - so always run regression on critical fields after quantization.
07:28 Jared: Let's recap next steps: Redwood sends eval plan + scoring sheet by Monday 2025-11-10; NorthStar provides anonymized sample dataset by 2025-11-12; schedule a benchmark run week of 2025-11-17. Security docs delivered by 2025-11-09. Any objections?
07:42 Ellen: No objections. We'll aim for those dates.
07:45 Sasha: I will send the KMS/contact details to Lena.
07:48 Lena: Thanks - we'll follow up with the onboarding checklist and pre-benchmark checklist.
07:52 Marc: One more small ask - can you include a few example failure cases that would require escalation?
07:56 Priya: Yes - we'll include example Type A failure cases in the plan with remediation playbooks.
08:02 Jared: Great. We'll close there. Thanks everyone.
08:05 Ellen: Thanks all.

[End of transcript]
